questions.enonce_markdown: How do humans differ from other mammals? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Humans (*Homo sapiens*) are mammals, but they differ from other mammals in the following ways (any six):

1. Humans walk **upright on two legs** (bipedal), with an S-shaped backbone, a broad pelvis and arched feet; most other mammals walk on four legs.
2. Humans have a **much larger and more highly developed brain** (especially the cerebrum), which gives greater intelligence, reasoning and memory.
3. Humans can use **articulate speech** and complex language to communicate.
4. Humans have **opposable thumbs** and a precision grip, so they can make and use tools.
5. Humans have **very little body hair**, whereas other mammals are usually covered with fur.
6. Humans have a **flatter face, smaller jaws and a chin**; other mammals have a protruding snout.
7. Humans have a **longer period of childhood**, with long parental care and dependence.
8. Humans can **control fire, make clothes, build houses and farm**, and so modify the environment to suit themselves.
9. Humans are **omnivorous**, while many other mammals are herbivores or carnivores.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State two functions of each of the following cell organelles:

(i) Nucleus (ii) Mitochondrion (iii) Endoplasmic reticulum (iv) Lysosome *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Nucleus:**
   1. It controls all the activities of the cell (it contains the chromosomes with the genes).
   2. It carries the hereditary information (DNA) and passes it to daughter cells during cell division.

(ii) **Mitochondrion:**
   1. It is the site of aerobic respiration, where food (glucose) is oxidised.
   2. It releases energy in the form of ATP for the activities of the cell.

(iii) **Endoplasmic reticulum:**
   1. Rough ER (with ribosomes) is the site of protein synthesis.
   2. It transports materials through the cell (smooth ER also makes lipids and steroids).

(iv) **Lysosome:**
   1. It contains digestive enzymes that digest worn-out cell organelles and food particles taken into the cell.
   2. It destroys bacteria engulfed by the cell (and breaks down the cell after its death).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define each of the following terms:

(i) Diffusion (ii) Osmosis (iii) Active transport. *(2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Diffusion** is the net movement of molecules or ions from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement. It needs no energy.

(ii) **Osmosis** is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to a region of lower water potential (concentrated solution) through a partially (selectively) permeable membrane.

(iii) **Active transport** is the movement of molecules or ions across a cell membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, against the concentration gradient. It needs energy (ATP) from respiration and carrier proteins.
